raw_response:
I am getting older now, so on 4.5 mu I do not want to take big risks. I will still do wheat and maize, same as most people here. That way the land does not stay idle, and even if one crop is not so good, the other can still bring some money. I only finished primary school, so I do not calculate too finely. I mostly look at what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can put in without feeling too tight. We have only 2 people at home and some off-farm work, so I keep the plan simple, use the well when the crop really needs it, and do not spend too much on extra inputs unless I see a clear problem.

decision.reasoning_summary: I keep wheat-maize on all 4.5 mu because this is the safest way for me. I do not want to gamble with a new crop at my age. I use a moderate amount of fertilizer, not the highest, because cash is limited and there are only 2 people in the household, but I also do not want to under-apply and lose yield. For wheat I will irrigate twice if needed, mainly around wintering recovery and jointing, and for maize I will use the well once if the summer rain is not enough. I follow the local planting time and what nearby farmers do, and I keep labor-saving methods because some family labor is tied up off-farm.
